claim: Multi-scale phase contrast x-ray tomography can be used for virtual histology and histopathology of unstained lung tissue from Covid-19 patients.
source: We present a three-dimensional (3D) approach for virtual histology and histopathology based on multi-scale phase contrast x-ray tomography, and use this to investigate the parenchymal architecture of unstained lung tissue from patients who succumbed to Covid-19.
evidence: The abstract directly states the approach and its application to Covid-19 lung tissue.

claim: The multi-scale phase contrast x-ray tomography approach allows for segmentation of individual cells in autopsy samples with a maximum cross section of 8 mm.
source: By combining parallel and cone beam geometry, autopsy samples with a maximum cross section of 8 mm are scanned and reconstructed at a resolution and image quality, which allows for the segmentation of individual cells.
evidence: The abstract describes the technical capability achieved in the study.

claim: The cone beam geometry achieves a minimum voxel size of 167 nm in regions-of-interest.
source: Using the zoom capability of the cone beam geometry, regions-of-interest are reconstructed with a minimum voxel size of 167 nm.
evidence: The abstract specifies the resolution achieved with the cone beam geometry.

claim: The approach enables 3D visualization of diffuse alveolar damage (DAD) with hyaline membrane formation.
source: We exemplify the capability of this approach by 3D visualization of diffuse alveolar damage (DAD) with its prominent hyaline membrane formation
evidence: The abstract states this as a demonstrated capability of the method.

claim: The approach allows mapping of the 3D distribution and density of lymphocytes infiltrating the tissue.
source: by mapping the 3D distribution and density of lymphocytes infiltrating the tissue
evidence: The abstract describes this as an exemplified capability.

claim: The approach provides histograms of characteristic distances from tissue interior to the closest air compartment.
source: and by providing histograms of characteristic distances from tissue interior to the closest air compartment.
evidence: The abstract lists this as a quantitative output of the method.

claim: Severe progression of Covid-19 is frequently accompanied by clinical acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and respiratory failure.
source: Severe progression of the 2019 coronavirus disease (Covid-19) is frequently accompanied by the clinical acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and respiratory failure, an organ manifestation responsible for the majority of Covid-19 fatalities.
evidence: This is stated as established clinical knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Lung injury associated with ARDS can be detected by radiographic chest imaging and clinical computed tomography (CT).
source: Lung injury associated with ARDS can be readily detected by radiographic chest imaging and clinical computed tomography (CT), which have assisted the diagnosis and management of Covid-19 patients (Lee et al., 2020; Shi et al., 2020; Chung et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Peripheral lung ground-glass opacities are the main radiological hallmark of ARDS.
source: Here, so-called peripheral lung ground-glass opacities are the main radiological hallmark of ARDS
evidence: This is stated as established radiological knowledge.

claim: Ground-glass opacities can be linked to the histological observation of diffuse alveolar damage (DAD) with edema, hemorrhage, and intraalveolar fibrin deposition.
source: and can be linked to the histological observation of diffuse alveolar damage (DAD) with edema, hemorrhage, and intraalveolar fibrin deposition (Ackermann et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ackermann et al., 2020.

claim: DAD findings have been reported for infections by MERS-CoV, SARS-CoV, and influenza viruses.
source: These findings have also been reported for infections by Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV), SARS-CoV, and influenza viruses.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about respiratory viral infections.

claim: Distinctive features of pulmonary involvement of Covid-19 include severe endothelial injury associated with the presence of intracellular virions and inflammation.
source: Distinctive features of pulmonary involvement of Covid-19 include severe endothelial injury associated with the presence of intracellular virions and inflammation, disrupted cellular membranes, as well as widespread thrombosis with microangiopathy.
evidence: This is stated as a distinctive feature of Covid-19 based on prior research.

claim: Alveolar capillary microthrombi were found to be nine times as prevalent in patients with Covid-19 as in patients with H1N1 influenza A virus.
source: As reported in Ackermann et al., 2020, alveolar capillary microthrombi were found to be nine times as prevalent in patients with Covid-19 as in patients with the also very aggressive H1N1 influenza A virus, also referred to as swine flu.
evidence: This claim is explicitly attributed to Ackermann et al., 2020.

claim: In Covid-19 lungs, intussusceptive angiogenesis was 2.7 times as high as in lungs of patients with H1N1 influenza A.
source: Importantly, in Covid-19 lungs, a specific variant of new vessel growth - intussusceptive angiogenesis - was significantly more prevalent, that is, 2.7 times as high as in lungs of patients with H1N1 influenza A.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from prior research (implied from Ackermann et al., 2020).

claim: Histomorphological assessment of formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue stained with haematoxylin and eosin represents the gold standard in histological diagnostics of non-neoplastic lung diseases.
source: Histomorphological assessment of formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue stained with haematoxylin and eosin still represents the gold standard in histological diagnostics of non-neoplastic lung diseases, including DAD and virus induced pneumonia.
evidence: This is stated as established practice in histopathology.

claim: Digitalization, visualization and quantification of morphological changes associated with Covid-19 require both high resolution and the capability to screen larger volumes.
source: In order to unravel the corresponding pathophysiology of the lungs, digitalization, visualization and quantification of the morphological changes associated with Covid-19 represent a key challenge, and require both high resolution and the capability to screen larger volumes.
evidence: This is stated as a logical requirement based on the nature of the problem.

claim: Imaging the intricate three-dimensional tissue architecture of the lung and its pathological alterations on multiple length scales calls for 3D extensions of well-established histology techniques.
source: For this reason, imaging the intricate three-dimensional (3D) tissue architecture of the lung and its pathological alterations on multiple length scales calls for 3D extensions of well-established histology techniques.
evidence: This is stated as a logical conclusion from the previous statement.

claim: Integration of 3D morphological information with well-established histology techniques can provide a substantial asset for unraveling the pathophysiology of SARS-Cov-2 infections.
source: Our work is based on the assertion that integration of 3D morphological information with well-established histology techniques can provide a substantial asset for unraveling the pathophysiology of SARS-Cov-2 infections.
evidence: This is stated as the underlying hypothesis of the work.

claim: X-ray tomography data were collected from the same autopsies that were previously studied by immunohistochemical analysis and measurements of gene expression.
source: To this end, we have collected x-ray tomography data from the same autopsies, which were previously studied by immunohistochemical analysis and measurements of gene expression (Ackermann et al., 2020).
evidence: This describes the sample source and its relationship to prior studies.

claim: The study investigated postmortem lung samples from six patients who succumbed from Covid-19.
source: Here we present first results obtained from the postmortem lung samples of six patients who succumbed from Covid-19.
evidence: This describes the sample set used in the study.

claim: Propagation-based x-ray phase-contrast tomography (PC-CT) offers full 3D visualization with isotropic resolution without destructive slicing of the specimen.
source: In contrast to conventional histology based on thin sections, propagation-based x-ray phase-contrast tomography (PC-CT) offers a full 3D visualization with isotropic resolution and without destructive slicing of the specimen (Ding et al., 2019; Dejea et al., 2019; Saccomano et al., 2018; Töpperwien et al., 2018; Khimchenko et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: For hard x-rays, the real-valued decrement δ is several orders of magnitude higher in soft biological tissues than β, which accounts for absorption.
source: Phase contrast capitalizes on the fact that for hard x-rays, the real-valued decrement δ is several orders of magnitude higher in soft biological tissues than β, which accounts for absorption (Nugent, 2010)
evidence: This is stated as established physics knowledge with a citation.

claim: Small contrast levels can be reconstructed by propagation imaging even at low fluence.
source: and that small contrast levels can be reconstructed by propagation imaging even at low fluence (Jahn et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Jahn et al., 2017.

claim: Contrast is formed by transformation of the phase shifts into measurable intensity variations by self-interference of the exit wave during free-space propagation between sample and detector.
source: Contrast is formed by transformation of the phase shifts into measurable intensity variations by self-interference of the exit wave during free-space propagation between sample and detector (Paganin and Nugent, 1998; Cloetens et al., 1999).
evidence: This describes the physical mechanism with supporting citations.

claim: Phase contrast tomography has been demonstrated as an advantageous imaging technique for lung imaging up to macroscopic scales.
source: For lung imaging it has already been demonstrated as an advantageous imaging technique up to macroscopic scales (Parsons et al., 2008; Stahr et al., 2016; Morgan et al., 2020), including live animal models of respiratory diseases.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Propagation-based phase contrast can reach a resolution below optical microscopy.
source: But in contrast to other full-field phase contrast techniques, e.g. based on grating interferometry or analyzer crystals, it can also reach a resolution below optical microscopy (Khimchenko et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Khimchenko et al., 2018.

claim: Phase contrast x-ray tomography can probe small electron density variations of unstained tissue embedded in paraffin, ethanol, or aqueous buffer.
source: In this work we exploit both the high resolution capability of PC-CT and the fact that its phase sensitivity is high enough to probe the small electron density variations of unstained tissue, embedded in paraffin, ethanol, or even aqueous buffer (Töpperwien et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Töpperwien et al., 2019.

claim: The multi-scale phase contrast x-ray tomography was implemented at the GINIX endstation of the beamline P10/PETRA III (DESY, Hamburg).
source: Scale-bridging and dynamic ROI selection in close spatial and temporal proximity was implemented with dedicated instrumentation the GINIX endstation of the beamline P10/PETRA III (DESY, Hamburg) (Salditt et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes the experimental facility used.

claim: Parallel beam tomography covers a large field of view with a pixel size of 650 nm.
source: (i) Parallel beam tomography, covering a large field of view (FOV), with a pixel size of 650 nm.
evidence: This describes the technical specifications of one imaging mode.

claim: Cone beam geometry provides mode filtering, enhanced spatial coherence and smooth wavefronts based on advanced x-ray waveguide optics.
source: (ii) Cone beam geometry for recording of highly magnified holograms, based on advanced x-ray waveguide optics, providing mode filtering, that is, enhanced spatial coherence and smooth wavefronts.
evidence: This describes the technical features of the cone beam geometry.

claim: The effective pixel size in cone beam geometry can be adjusted in the range 10 nm–300 nm based on geometrical magnification.
source: Based on the geometrical magnification, the effective pixel size can be adjusted in the range 10 nm–300 nm.
evidence: This describes the technical capability of the cone beam setup.

claim: The x-ray optics and geometric parameters allow reaching extremely small Fresnel numbers F in the deeply holographic regime.
source: Further, using this particular optics, together with appropriate choices of photon energy and geometric parameters, we can reach extremely small Fresnel numbers F of the deeply holographic regime, well below the typical range exploited at other nano-tomography instruments.
evidence: This describes a technical advantage of the setup.

claim: The deeply holographic regime offers the advantage of highest phase sensitivity sufficient to probe small electron density variations of unstained tissue at relatively low dose.
source: This offers the advantage of highest phase sensitivity sufficient to even probe the small electron density variations of unstained tissue, at relatively low dose (Hagemann and Salditt, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Hagemann and Salditt, 2018.

claim: Advanced phase retrieval methods including non-linear generalizations of the CTF-method based on Tikhonov regularization were used.
source: To exploit this sensitivity, we use advanced phase retrieval methods including non-linear generalizations of the CTF-method (Cloetens et al., 1999) based on Tikhonov regularization (Lohse et al., 2020).
evidence: This describes the computational methods used with supporting citations.

claim: Sample I showed DAD with focal formation of hyaline membranes adjacent to the epithelial lining by conventional histopathological assessment.
source: By conventional histopathological assessment, the peribronchial alveolar parenchyma of sample I showed DAD with focal formation of hyaline membranes adjacent to the epithelial lining, moderate lymphocytic interstitial pneumonia and singular thrombi in small pulmonary veins.
evidence: This describes the histopathological findings for sample I.

claim: Sample I showed moderate lymphocytic interstitial pneumonia and singular thrombi in small pulmonary veins.
source: By conventional histopathological assessment, the peribronchial alveolar parenchyma of sample I showed DAD with focal formation of hyaline membranes adjacent to the epithelial lining, moderate lymphocytic interstitial pneumonia and singular thrombi in small pulmonary veins.
evidence: This describes the histopathological findings for sample I.

claim: Sample I showed moderate hypertrophy of the muscular media in smaller pre- and post-capillary blood vessels with desquamation of the endothelial cell layer.
source: There is a moderate hypertrophy of the muscular media in smaller pre- and post-capillary blood vessels with desquamation of the endothelial cell layer as well as mild centrilobular emphysema (original magnification 100×).
evidence: This describes the histopathological findings for sample I.

claim: Sample II showed peribronchial alveolar parenchyma with hyperemia of capillary and post-capillary blood vessels by histomorphological analysis.
source: Histomorphological analysis shows peribronchial alveolar parenchyma with hyperemia of capillary and post-capillary blood vessels, as well as a moderate centrilobular emphysema (original magnification 100×).
evidence: This describes the histopathological findings for sample II.

claim: Sample III consists of peribronchial alveolar parenchyma showing prominent multifocal neutrophilic capillaritis.
source: The sample consists of peribronchial alveolar parenchyma showing prominent multifocal neutrophilic capillaritis as well as a moderate centrilobular emphysema (original magnification 100×).
evidence: This describes the histopathological findings for sample III.

claim: Sample IV showed peribronchial alveolar parenchyma with marked lymphocytic interstitial pneumonia, multifocal venous thrombi and focal intraalveolar fibrin deposition in terms of DAD.
source: Histomorphological analysis shows peribronchial alveolar parenchyma with marked lymphocytic interstitial pneumonia, multifocal venous thrombi and focal intraalveolar fibrin deposition in terms of DAD.
evidence: This describes the histopathological findings for sample IV.

claim: Sample V consists of peribronchial alveolar parenchyma showing massive lymphocytic interstitial pneumonia with ubiquitous hyaline membranes superimposed on the alveolar walls.
source: By conventional histological assessment, Sample V consists of peribronchial alveolar parenchyma showing massive lymphocytic interstitial pneumonia with ubiquitous hyaline membranes superimposed on the alveolar walls, neutrophilic capillaritis and multifocal post-capillary thrombi in terms of severe DAD.
evidence: This describes the histopathological findings for sample V.

claim: Sample V showed bronchialized alveolar epithelial cells with cytopathic changes and multifocal desquamation.
source: Furthermore, bronchialized alveolar epithelial cells show cytopathic changes and multifocal desquamation, as does alveolar macrophages.
evidence: This describes the histopathological findings for sample V.

claim: Sample V showed focal accumulation of intraalveolar neutrophilic granulocytes in the sense of a florid bronchopneumonia.
source: Focally, accumulation of intraalveolar neutrophilic granulocytes in the sense of a florid bronchopneumonia can be observed (original magnification 100×).
evidence: This describes the histopathological findings for sample V.

claim: Different cell types as macrophages, T-cells or erythrocytes can be distinguished in the zoom tomogram of sample V.
source: Noteworthy, different cell types as macrophages, T-cells or erythrocytes can be distinguished in the zoom tomogram.
evidence: This describes the capability demonstrated in the high-resolution data.

claim: Sample VI showed peribronchial alveolar parenchyma with lymphocytic interstitial pneumonitis and a singular thrombus in a small vein.
source: Histomorphological analysis shows peribronchial alveolar parenchyma with lymphocytic interstitial pneumonitis and a singular thrombus in a small vein.
evidence: This describes the histopathological findings for sample VI.

claim: Sample VI showed widened interstitium of the alveolar septae by myogenic metaplasia.
source: The interstitium of the alveolar septae is widened by myogenic metaplasia.
evidence: This describes the histopathological findings for sample VI.

claim: Sample VI showed centrilobular emphysema and anthracosis adjacent to the affected areas.
source: Adjacent, centrilobular emphysema and anthracosis are observed.
evidence: This describes the histopathological findings for sample VI.

claim: The bronchial mucosa in sample VI shows varying degrees of lymphocytic inflammation in the sense of chronic bronchitis/bronchiolitis.
source: The bronchial mucosa shows varying degrees of lymphocytic inflammation in the sense of chronic bronchitis/bronchiolitis (original magnification 100×).
evidence: This describes the histopathological findings for sample VI.

claim: 3D histology analysis based on x-ray tomography and light sheet microscopy is required to quantitatively understand functional tissue properties based on its 3D architecture.
source: More generally, we claim that 3D histology analysis based on x-ray tomography and light sheet microscopy (Power and Huisken, 2017) is required to quantitatively understand functional tissue properties based on its 3D architecture.
evidence: This is stated as a general claim with a supporting citation.

claim: Patient II has the highest surface area volume-ratios among the six samples.
source: E.g. patient II has the highest surface area volume-ratios while sample I and VI have a relatively low specific surface.
evidence: This is stated based on the quantitative analysis presented in Table 1.

claim: Samples I and VI have relatively low specific surface compared to other samples.
source: E.g. patient II has the highest surface area volume-ratios while sample I and VI have a relatively low specific surface.
evidence: This is stated based on the quantitative analysis presented in Table 1.

claim: Larger characteristic lengths may be indicative of inflammation and the formation of hyaline membranes.
source: Larger characteristic lengths may also be indicative of inflammation and the formation of hyaline membranes, which will be evaluated in the following based on ROI and high-resolution reconstructions.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the quantitative metrics.

claim: Multi-scale x-ray phase contrast tomography can augment pathohistology of the lung to full three dimensions.
source: In summary, we have demonstrated that multi-scale x-ray phase contrast tomography can firstly augment pathohistology of the lung to full three dimensions, and secondly provide a link between microscopic and macroscopic scales.
evidence: This is stated as a summary conclusion of the study.

claim: Multi-scale x-ray phase contrast tomography provides a link between microscopic and macroscopic scales.
source: In summary, we have demonstrated that multi-scale x-ray phase contrast tomography can firstly augment pathohistology of the lung to full three dimensions, and secondly provide a link between microscopic and macroscopic scales.
evidence: This is stated as a summary conclusion of the study.

claim: Characteristic morphological changes associated with DAD such as hyaline membranes and pronounced inflammation have been imaged in three dimensions for the first time in Covid-19.
source: For the first time, characteristic morphological changes associated with DAD such as hyaline membranes and pronounced inflammation have been imaged in three dimensions, in particular in Covid-19, the most severe pandemic which mankind has faced for decades.
evidence: This is stated as a novel achievement of the study.

claim: The study was conducted in FFPE material, a fixation method established for well over a century and ubiquitously available.
source: Moreover, we conducted our study in FFPE material, a fixation method established for well over a century and ubiquitously available.
evidence: This describes the sample preparation method used.

claim: 3D histology enables the accurate determination of cell densities.
source: This enables the accurate determination of cell densities, the quantification of morphological parameters such as the distance metrics shown in Figure 6, and tracing of blood vessels.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of 3D histology.

claim: 3D histology enables the quantification of morphological parameters such as distance metrics.
source: This enables the accurate determination of cell densities, the quantification of morphological parameters such as the distance metrics shown in Figure 6, and tracing of blood vessels.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of 3D histology with reference to Figure 6.

claim: 3D histology enables tracing of blood vessels.
source: This enables the accurate determination of cell densities, the quantification of morphological parameters such as the distance metrics shown in Figure 6, and tracing of blood vessels.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of 3D histology.

claim: Standard histology and immunohistochemical staining can inform more precisely on the biomolecular origin of the structure.
source: Standard histology and in particular immunohistochemical staining, on the other hand, can inform us more precisely on the biomolecular origin of the structure, while immunostaining coupled with x-ray contrast agents is not yet within reach.
evidence: This is stated as a complementary advantage of conventional histology.

claim: Immunostaining coupled with x-ray contrast agents is not yet within reach.
source: Standard histology and in particular immunohistochemical staining, on the other hand, can inform us more precisely on the biomolecular origin of the structure, while immunostaining coupled with x-ray contrast agents is not yet within reach.
evidence: This is stated as a current limitation.

claim: PC-CT is nondestructive, allowing histology to be performed on well-chosen sections after the scan.
source: Importantly, since PC-CT is nondestructive, histology can be performed on well-chosen sections after the scan, see Appendix 1.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of the method.

claim: Higher resolution could be achieved by further geometric zooms, waveguide optics with higher numerical aperture, in combination with pixel detector technology.
source: On the side of imaging technology and exploitation, there is still ample room for improvement: higher resolution could be achieved by further geometric zooms, waveguide optics with higher numerical aperture, in combination with pixel detector technology, and further improvements in holographic reconstruction.
evidence: This is stated as a potential future improvement.

claim: Optimized recording and data flow is a larger bottleneck than photons and optics for extending the field of view.
source: To this end, optimized recording and data flow is a larger bottleneck than photons and optics, in particular since 4th generation synchrotron radiation sources are about to deliver unprecedented brilliance.
evidence: This is stated as an assessment of current limitations.

claim: Specific labels for different cell types and 3D immunostaining coupled to radiocontrast agents should be developed.
source: Finally, in view of exploitation and information gain, specific labels for different cell types and 3D immunostaining coupled to radiocontrast agents should be developed.
evidence: This is stated as a future development goal.

claim: Lung offers an advantage over other tissue in view of volume accessibility and label diffusivity.
source: Here, lung offers an advantage over other tissue in view of volume accessibility and label diffusivity.
evidence: This is stated as a property of lung tissue relevant for future development.

claim: Tracing of capillaries is an important next step in view of unraveling the role of intussusceptive angiogenesis in Covid-19.
source: Tracing of capillaries is an obvious important next step, in view of unraveling the role of intussusceptive angiogenesis in Covid-19 (Ackermann et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated as a future research direction with a citation.

claim: The current data are likely to already provide clues about intussusceptive angiogenesis once more advanced segmentation approaches based on machine learning are applied.
source: The current data, which are made fully available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.3892637, are likely to already provide such clues once that more advanced segmentation approaches based on machine learning are applied.
evidence: This is stated as a speculation about the potential of the data.

claim: Phase contrast tomography of lung biopsies could in future help diagnosis and treatment.
source: Possibly, phase contrast tomography of lung biopsies could in future also help diagnosis and treatment.
evidence: This is stated as a potential future application.

claim: All patients suffered from hypertension and were treated with RAAS interacting drugs.
source: All patients suffered from hypertension and were treated with RAAS (renin-angiotensin-aldosterone-system) interacting drugs.
evidence: This describes a common clinical characteristic of all patients.

claim: Heterogeneous ground glass and consolidation were observed in all patients' clinical CT scans.
source: Heterogeneous ground glass and consolidation were observed in all patients clinical CT scans and the cause of death was also related to respiratory failure in each patient (patient IV cardio-respiratory failure).
evidence: This describes a common radiological finding in all patients.

claim: The cause of death was related to respiratory failure in each patient.
source: Heterogeneous ground glass and consolidation were observed in all patients clinical CT scans and the cause of death was also related to respiratory failure in each patient (patient IV cardio-respiratory failure).
evidence: This describes the cause of death for all patients.

claim: Parallel beam configuration results in a FOV of 1.6 mm sampled at a pixel size of 650 nm.
source: Recordings with the unfocused quasi-parallel beam illumination and a high resolution microscope detection system, resulting in in a FOV of 1.6 mm sampled at a pixel size of 650 nm.
evidence: This describes the technical specifications of the parallel beam configuration.

claim: Cone beam configuration results in a FOV of 0.4 mm sampled at a pixel size of about 167 nm.
source: Holographic recordings with the divergent and coherence filtered beam emanating from a compound focusing system composed of a Kirkpatrick-Baez (KB) mirrors system and an x-ray waveguide, resulting in a FOV of 0.4 mm sampled at a pixel size of about 167 nm (depending on exact geometry).
evidence: This describes the technical specifications of the cone beam configuration.

claim: Overview scans were composed of up to 20 individual tomograms depending on tissue size.
source: To this end a 3.5 mm biopsy punch was taken from the multi-sample tissue block, and then scanned in a stitching-mode yielding a large overview reconstruction, composed of up to 20 individual tomograms (depending on tissue size).
evidence: This describes the stitching approach used for overview scans.

claim: Phase retrieval was performed using both linearised single step CTF-approach and non-linear generalizations of the CTF-method based on Tikhonov regularization (NL-CTF).
source: Phase retrieval was performed from dark and empty beam corrected holograms, using both linearised single step CTF-approach (Cloetens et al., 1999; Turner et al., 2004), and non-linear generalizations of the CTF-method based on Tikhonov regularization (NL-CTF), using our code package HoloTomoToolbox as described and deposited (Lohse et al., 2020).
evidence: This describes the phase retrieval methods used with supporting citations.

claim: Both CTF and NL-CTF implementations can be augmented by imposing support and range constraints when needed.
source: Importantly, both CTF and NL-CTF implementations can be augmented by imposing support and range constraints, when needed.
evidence: This describes additional capabilities of the phase retrieval methods.

claim: Tomographic reconstruction was carried out with the MATLAB implemented iradon-function for the parallel geometry.
source: After phase reconstruction of all projections, the tomographic reconstruction was carried out with the MATLAB implemented iradon-function (Ram-Lak filter) for the parallel geometry
evidence: This describes the reconstruction method used for parallel beam data.

claim: Tomographic reconstruction was carried out with the FDK-function of the ASTRA toolbox for the cone beam geometry.
source: and with the FDK-function of the ASTRA toolbox (van Aarle et al., 2015; van Aarle et al., 2016) for the cone beam geometry.
evidence: This describes the reconstruction method used for cone beam data with supporting citations.

claim: The extra information provided by 360° scans was used to mask out pixels with artifacts and replace them with values of the opposing projection.
source: To correct for this, the extra information provided by 360° scans was used to mask out the corresponding pixels and replace them with values of the opposing projection.
evidence: This describes a correction method for ring artifacts.

claim: Stitching of reconstructions from different tomographic scans was performed using Miettinen et al., 2019.
source: Stitching of reconstructions from different tomographic scans was performed using (Miettinen et al., 2019).
evidence: This describes the stitching method with a citation.

claim: The tissue was segmented from the surrounding paraffin using the segmentation software Ilastik.
source: The 3D-reconstructions were first binned (2 × 2 × 2), and the tissue was then segmented from the surrounding paraffin using the segmentation software Ilastik (Berg et al., 2019), which was then further refined with MATLAB.
evidence: This describes the segmentation method with a citation.

claim: An automatic and parameter-controlled algorithm denoted as BlobFinder was used to identify lymphocytes.
source: To this end, an automatic and parameter-controlled algorithm denoted as BlobFinder was used (arivis AG, Germany).
evidence: This describes the algorithm used for lymphocyte segmentation.

claim: Lymphocytes appear denser compared to the nuclei of macrophages in the tomographic reconstructions.
source: For the unbinned datasets, a distinction between lymphocytes and the nuclei of the macrophages was made based on the difference in electron density. In the tomographic reconstructions, the lymphocytes appear denser compared to the nuclei of the macrophages.
evidence: This describes an observation used for cell type discrimination.

claim: Only structures with a sphericity higher than 0.55 were included in the lymphocyte segmentation.
source: Further, nuclei from endothelial cells and parts of the capillaries filled with blood residues were excluded based on their elongated shape. Only structures with a sphericity higher than 0.55 were included.
evidence: This describes a criterion used in the segmentation algorithm.

claim: The reconstruction volumes are visualized in Video 1.
source: The entire reconstruction volume is visualized in Video 1.
evidence: This references a video showing the reconstruction data.

claim: Figure 7 illustrates the aggregation of hyaline membrane in the vicinity of a single alveole.
source: Figure 7 illustrates the aggregation of hyaline membrane in the vicinity of a single alveole.
evidence: This describes what Figure 7 shows.

claim: Volumetric renderings demonstrate particular attachment of fibrin to the alveolar walls.
source: Volumetric renderings in Figure 7a and b demonstrate particular attachment of fibrin to the alveolar walls.
evidence: This describes an observation from the volumetric renderings in Figure 7.

claim: In cases of severe hyaline membrane formation, this pathological alteration can be tracked throughout the volume.
source: In cases of severe hyaline membrane formation as for this patient, this pathological alteration can be tracked throughout the volume Figure 7c–e.
evidence: This describes a capability demonstrated in Figure 7.

claim: Figure 7g exemplifies a direct connection of hyaline membranes to the vasculature.
source: In the 3D-context, their locations with respect to blood vessels can be inspected, see Figure 7g, which exemplifies a direct connection of hyaline membranes to the vasculature.
evidence: This describes what Figure 7g shows.
